question.text: The product of a <math><mn>9</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>4</mn></math> matrix and a <math><mn>4</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>9</mn></math> matrix contains a variable <math><mi>x</mi></math> in exactly two places. If <math><mi>D</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> is the determinant of the matrix product such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>D</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mn>0</mn></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>D</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>D</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></math>, then <math><mi>D</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is equal to

solution.text:
Let, the order of matrix A is 9×4 and matrix B is 4×9
Dx=AB= a polynomial of degree 2 as it has x at 2 places.
Let, Dx=ax2+bx+c
D0=c=1
D-1=a-b+c=1⇒a-b=0
D2=4a+2b+c=7⇒4a+2b=6
⇒2a+b=3
Solving these two equations, we get, 

 a=1,b=1
⇒Dx=x2+x+1
⇒D-2=4-2+1=3
